rows.title: Housing starts and construction data for October 2026
rows.summary: Canada's federal housing agency, CMHC, reported that the seasonally adjusted annual rate of housing starts fell 2% in October 2026 to 244,558 units, from a revised 250,072 in September, and the six-month trend fell 1.7% to 246,231. Ontario's trend fell about 8% and Toronto's about 10%, while Quebec and Alberta edged up and Montreal and Vancouver gained on more multi-unit (apartment and condo) starts. Actual starts in centres of 10,000+ people were up 6% from October 2025, but January-to-October starts were still 3% lower than a year earlier at 192,023 units. Pending starts (projects approved but not yet started) fell 3% to 139,592, and units under construction slipped 0.6%, which points to fewer new homes in the pipeline. CMHC deputy chief economist Kevin Hughes warned that building too little during the current downturn could hurt affordability later, once demand recovers.
rows.fact: The national annual pace of housing starts fell 2% to 244,558 units in October 2026, and the six-month trend dropped 1.7% to 246,231, led by declines in Ontario, B.C. and Atlantic Canada. Completions in larger centres jumped 24% to 21,621, while pending starts fell 3%.
rows.outlook: CMHC says the drop in pending starts signals some near-term softness in construction, and under-building now is a risk to future affordability.
rows.why: 주택 착공이라는 '공급' 지표가 왜 미래의 집값과 임대료를 좌우하는지, 경기 침체기에 공급을 줄이면 수요가 회복될 때 어떤 문제가 생기는지 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a supply indicator like housing starts shapes future home prices and rents, and what problems arise when building slows in a downturn and demand later recovers.
rows.term_def: A way to report one month's data as if that pace lasted a full year, with normal seasonal swings (like less building in winter) removed. That lets you compare different months fairly.
rows.note: Official CMHC release, Nov 17, 2026, 8:15 a.m. ET (22:15 KST); full body read on newswire.ca. Headline figures (244,558; revised 250,072) match separate Nov 17 reports. No economist reaction to this release was out yet, so C is a same-day analysis of the housing supply gap.

opinion.title: Canada housing starts can absorb Budget 2026 growth, gap persists
opinion.author: Liezel Once
opinion.summary: This analysis draws on a Rentals.ca report that compares Canada's construction pace with its population growth, using StatCan population estimates and CMHC data. At about 240,000 starts a year, Canada can house roughly 500,000 new residents, and every 2027 scenario under Budget 2026's immigration plan (177,000 to 440,000 added people) falls below that level. Even so, the cumulative housing shortfall is still about 571,000 units (down from roughly 780,000 in mid-2024), and CMHC estimates 187,000 to 238,000 extra units a year are needed to restore affordability. Asking rents have fallen year over year for 25 straight months, but they are starting to rise again in Toronto and Vancouver, and falling condo presales will mean fewer completions in 2028-2029. CMHC chief economist Mathieu Laberge warns that cutting construction too sharply in a soft market could create future shortages.
opinion.why: 인구 증가(수요)와 주택 건설(공급)을 비교해 보면, 지금 임대료가 떨어지는 것이 왜 일시적일 수 있는지 수요·공급 원리로 이해할 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: By comparing population growth (demand) with homebuilding (supply), it explains through supply and demand why today's falling rents may only be temporary.

rows.title: Warsh grapples with AI's potential economic impact, steers clear of its inflation risk
rows.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh opened a one-day conference on AI and productivity at the San Francisco Fed on Monday, arguing that AI could speed up innovation and support economic growth well above its long-run average. He also named the downside risks: widespread job losses, and a sharp stock-market drop if the huge returns expected from AI infrastructure spending never show up. Warsh said nothing about the next interest-rate move and did not address inflation, even though last week's data showed inflation speeding up in October and several of his colleagues now back more rate hikes, possibly in December. Many Fed officials argue that building data centers is pushing up demand and prices for chips, electronic parts, electricity and copper, and October smartphone prices rose at a record pace. This puts the Fed chair's view that AI is a supply-side productivity boom at odds with colleagues who see it adding to demand-driven inflation right now.
rows.fact: On Nov 16 Warsh told a San Francisco Fed conference that AI could boost growth, and he listed risks including job losses and a market drop if AI investment disappoints. He gave no signal on rates and did not mention inflation, although October data showed inflation accelerating and many rate-setters favor further hikes.
rows.outlook: Several Fed officials expect another rate increase as early as the December meeting, but Warsh did not commit to one.
rows.why: AI가 생산성을 높여 물가를 낮출지, 아니면 투자 수요로 물가를 끌어올릴지를 둘러싼 연준 내부 논쟁을 통해 공급 충격과 수요 충격의 차이를 배울 수 있다.
rows.why_en: The Fed's internal debate over whether AI will lower inflation through higher productivity or raise it through investment demand teaches the difference between supply-side and demand-side shocks.
rows.term_def: How much output (goods and services) an economy produces per worker or per hour of work; when it rises, an economy can grow faster without pushing prices up.
rows.note: Fed chair speech within the last 24h, but not a policy decision or data release: October retail sales (due Nov 17, 8:30 ET) had not been published at research time. AP body (Nov 16, 12:22 ET = Nov 17 KST) cross-checked against a separate report of the same speech. Not a repeat: earlier editions covered Waller and Jefferson, not this Warsh speech.

opinion.title: Fed officials debate AI's impact on inflation and interest rates
opinion.author: Steve Thompson
opinion.summary: This news analysis explains that before he became Fed chair, Warsh argued the AI boom would help bring inflation down, but more than a dozen Fed colleagues, including two other Trump appointees, now say AI is pushing prices up. Governor Michelle Bowman puts AI investment at about a quarter of the excess inflation the Fed is fighting, roughly as large as tariffs or energy, and Governor Christopher Waller says AI-related energy price pressures will not fade soon. Warsh accepts that AI is raising chip prices but doubts it drives broad inflation, arguing a one-time price change is not necessarily inflationary. The piece says the key question is timing: if productivity gains arrive soon the Fed can be patient, but if they are years away (AEI's Michael Strain expects no earlier than 2028), rates may have to rise further, making credit cards, car loans and mortgages more expensive. It notes the Fed raised rates in September for the first time in over three years.
opinion.why: 같은 기술이 단기적으로는 수요를 늘려 물가를 올리고 장기적으로는 공급을 늘려 물가를 낮출 수 있다는 점이 금리 결정을 왜 어렵게 만드는지 보여준다.
opinion.why_en: It shows why rate decisions are hard when the same technology can raise prices in the short run by boosting demand but lower them in the long run by expanding supply.

rows.title: IMF raises Korea's 2026 growth forecast to 3.9% on AI chip boom
rows.summary: The International Monetary Fund raised its 2026 growth forecast for South Korea to 3.9% on Tuesday. That is 0.6 percentage points above its October projection, and the IMF also lifted its 2027 forecast to 3.3% from 2.8%. The upgrade came at the end of the IMF's annual consultation with Korean authorities, and the Fund credited booming AI-driven semiconductor exports, a rebound in investment and resilient consumption, while warning that the gains are concentrated in the tech sector. It expects inflation of 2.7% this year and 2.3% next year, both above the Bank of Korea's 2% target. Because the economy is running above its potential, the IMF advised further monetary tightening and a somewhat tighter fiscal stance, with targeted help for vulnerable households and businesses.
rows.fact: The IMF's 2026 forecast for Korea climbed from 1.9% in April to 2.6% in July, 3.3% in October and now 3.9%, above the OECD's 3.7%, the Bank of Korea's 3.3% and the government's 3.0%. The IMF welcomed the government's planned Future Response Fund as a tool for responding to economic cycles.
rows.outlook: The IMF expects tech-sector income to support wider consumption next year, but says uncertainty is high and risks to growth lean to the downside.
rows.why: 경제가 잠재성장률보다 빠르게 성장해 물가가 오를 때 왜 국제기구가 금리 인상과 재정 긴축을 권고하는지 이해할 수 있는 좋은 사례이기 때문이다.
rows.why_en: It is a clear example of why an international institution recommends higher interest rates and tighter government budgets when an economy grows faster than its potential and inflation rises.
rows.term_def: The fastest an economy can grow over time using its workers, capital and technology without pushing up inflation; growing faster than this for long tends to overheat prices.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (no major Korean government or Bank of Korea policy announcement or data release found for Nov 16-17; the IMF Article IV forecast announced in Seoul on Nov 17 KST was the biggest Korean economic story). Figures cross-checked against Korea JoongAng Daily and Seoul Economic Daily (Nov 17). No editorial on the forecast had appeared yet, so C is an analysis piece on the same chip-boom imbalance.

opinion.title: Not chipping in? Semiconductor boom fails to spread the wealth.
opinion.author: Cho Min-jun, Kang Ju-eon, Han Joon-woo, Jang Woo-jin and Choi Won-jun
opinion.summary: This long-form analysis looks at the problem the IMF flagged: Korea's record chip boom is not reaching most households. Chip exports hit $56.4 billion last month, up 259.4% from a year earlier, but capital-intensive, automated production adds profits without adding many jobs, and Bank of Korea data show employment in chip-related industries fell even as output jumped. The top 10 exporters made up 55.3% of exports in the second quarter, and gains go mostly to shareholders and high-income, high-asset households. A weak won and rising prices hit poorer families hardest, since they spend a much larger share on food, housing and medical costs. Economists quoted are split on how long the boom will last, and they call for policies that deliver real gains to ordinary citizens.
opinion.why: GDP 성장률이 높아도 그 혜택이 모든 사람에게 고르게 돌아가지 않을 수 있다는 점, 즉 성장과 분배의 차이를 생각해 보게 하기 때문이다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that a high GDP growth rate does not mean everyone benefits equally, which helps students think about the difference between growth and distribution.

rows.title: UK wage growth slows to 3.5% in three months to September
rows.summary: Official UK labour market data released on November 17 showed that regular pay growth, which leaves out bonuses, slowed to 3.5% a year in the three months to September, down from 3.7% and slightly below the 3.6% economists polled by Reuters had expected. Unemployment fell to 4.6% against expectations of 4.7%. Other signs were weaker: provisional tax data showed company payrolls fell by 34,000 in October, and job vacancies dropped by about 22,000 to 690,000 in the three months to October, the steepest quarterly fall since mid-2025. The figures matter for the Bank of England, which raised interest rates in November for the first time in more than three years and is watching whether this year's oil price surge, linked to the US-Iran war, is feeding into wages and wider business costs.
rows.fact: Regular wage growth eased to 3.5% (private sector steady at 3.1%), and unemployment fell to 4.6%. Payrolls fell by 34,000 in October and vacancies fell to 690,000. Reuters notes the headline wage figure is partly boosted by the timing of public-sector pay deals.
rows.outlook: Markets put roughly a 90% chance on another Bank of England rate rise in December and expect two or three more increases in 2027, while MPC member Megan Greene says surveys point to pay growth of at least 3.5% next year, too high for the 2% inflation target.
rows.why: 실업률은 떨어졌지만 일자리 공고와 급여 대상자 수는 줄어든 엇갈린 지표를 통해, 중앙은행이 임금 상승과 인플레이션 사이에서 금리를 어떻게 판단하는지 배울 수 있다.
rows.why_en: The mixed signals, with unemployment falling while vacancies and payrolls shrink, show how a central bank weighs wage growth against inflation when it sets interest rates.
rows.term_def: Pay growth after subtracting inflation. If your pay rises 3.5% but prices rise 3.3%, your real wage grows only about 0.2%, so you can buy just a little more than before.
rows.note: Official ONS labour market statistics, Nov 17, 2026 (07:00 GMT). Full Reuters text read on two republications; unemployment (4.6%) and vacancies (690,000) cross-checked with Personnel Today and FE News citing the ONS.

opinion.title: Unemployment falls but vacancies remain at 12-year low
opinion.author: Rob Moss (with expert commentary from CIPD, Institute for Employment Studies, Resolution Foundation and others)
opinion.summary: The piece gathers labour-market experts' reactions to the November ONS figures, and most see the drop in unemployment to a 17-month low of 4.6% as weaker than it looks. Naomi Clayton of the Institute for Employment Studies says the fall partly reflects changes to the ONS survey sample, and notes that vacancies, at 690,000, are at their lowest in 12 years outside the pandemic. CIPD's James Cockett calls the data a small relief but says hiring is still stalled because of cost and risk, and the Work Foundation describes a continuing jobs drought, with retail employment at its lowest since 1994. Inflation-adjusted pay grew only about 0.2%, and the Resolution Foundation expects real wage growth to turn negative by winter as inflation rises toward 5%, though it sees hopeful signs in rising payrolled employment among young adults.
opinion.why: 같은 통계를 두고 전문가들이 표본 문제, 고용 비용, 실질임금 등 서로 다른 관점에서 해석하는 모습을 보며 경제 지표를 비판적으로 읽는 법을 익힐 수 있다.
opinion.why_en: Seeing experts read the same data through different lenses, such as survey sampling, hiring costs and real wages, teaches students to read economic statistics critically.

rows.title: China's economy falters as factory output, retail sales undershoot expectations
rows.summary: China's National Bureau of Statistics reported on Nov 16 that October industrial output grew 4.8% year on year and retail sales only 0.4%, both below Reuters poll forecasts of 5.3% and 0.8% and slower than in September (5.5% and 1.1%). Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in January-October, a deeper drop than the 7.2% fall through September, and property investment plunged 21.6% as new home prices kept falling. Growth this year has leaned on an AI-driven export boom (Q3 GDP grew 4.5%), but households are holding back because of a soft job market, a long property slump and weak confidence. Even the October Golden Week holiday and the Singles Day shopping festival gave spending little lift. The data show strong foreign demand covering for weak domestic demand and put pressure on Beijing to decide whether more policy support is needed.
rows.fact: October industrial output rose 4.8% y/y and retail sales 0.4% y/y, both below forecasts. January-October fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% and property investment fell 21.6%. The urban unemployment rate eased to 5.1% from 5.2%, and an NBS spokesperson said exports will keep supporting growth.
rows.outlook: ANZ expects no new stimulus this year and sees full-year growth above 4.5%, while ING's Lynn Song says the economy needs more policy support.
rows.why: 수출은 호황인데 국내 소비와 투자가 부진한 중국 경제를 통해, 내수와 외수의 불균형이 경제 성장에 어떤 영향을 주는지 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: China's export boom alongside weak spending and investment at home shows how an imbalance between domestic and foreign demand shapes economic growth.
rows.term_def: Spending on long-lasting physical things like factories, machinery, roads and buildings. When it falls, firms and governments are building less for the future, which slows growth and job creation.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (official NBS data released Nov 16, about 11:00 KST, roughly 35 hours before this edition; no newer major Asian policy item found for Nov 17). Reuters figures checked against the official NBS release on english.www.gov.cn (IP +4.8%, retail +0.4%, FAI -8.1%, property investment -21.6%, unemployment 5.1%).

opinion.title: China's October domestic activity data disappoints across the board
opinion.author: Lynn Song (Chief Economist, Greater China, ING)
opinion.summary: Song says retail sales, investment and industrial output all missed expectations in October, a weak start to the fourth quarter. Inside retail, gold and jewellery sales fell 28.7% and car sales 21.4%, and he notes that government trade-in subsidies have turned from a tailwind into a headwind as their effect fades. He expects 2026 to be China's weakest year for consumption since the pandemic and calls weak consumer confidence the main obstacle. High-tech manufacturing grew 17.6%, but private investment shrank 11.4% and home prices have fallen for 41 straight months, though declines are slowing and tier-1 cities are recovering. He argues for new measures to support consumption: restoring household confidence by stabilizing asset prices and encouraging faster wage growth, plus cutting housing inventories so the property market can recover.
opinion.why: 소비자 신뢰, 자산 가격, 임금이 소비를 어떻게 좌우하는지 전문가의 분석으로 구체적으로 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: This expert analysis shows concretely how consumer confidence, asset prices and wages drive household spending.
